newsitem.title: UK: Tesco leads sector higher after upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Tesco leads sector higher after upgrade.

text.p: Shares in food retailers were mostly firmer on Thursday after encouraging profits from Wm. Morrison Supermarkets Plc, an upgrade on Tesco Plc and latest AGB market share figures all helped to renew interest in the sector.
Tesco led the advance to be up 5p at 338p after analysts at Kleinwort Benson upgraded the stock to a "hold" after previously giving "take profits" advice.
"The valuation is now more realistic and we felt that sentiment in the sector was about to turn," said industry analyst Simon Dunn.
Traders also noted switching activity from the financial sector into food retail stocks.
"There is some defensive value in the sector and there has been some switching around from some of the recent high flyers," said one.
Market sources said the latest survey by AGB Research was also well received.

During the four-week period up to March 19, ASDA Group's market share was up 7.5 percent. Tesco gained 6 percent whilst Sainsbury looked relatively flat and Safeway's market share apparently jumped by 14 percent.

"The Safeway and Sainsbury figures should really be disregarded this month," another analyst commented. "The figures are misleading and both companies report that their sales have not been so good or bad as the numbers suggest."
"Tesco and ASDA look to be continuing to grow their market share quite fast," he added.
Sainsbury was up 1p at 329-1/2p, ASDA gained 1-3/4p to 108-1/2 and Safeway was up 3-1/2p at 348p.
News that Wm Morrison had managed to post higher than expected annual profits was also positive for the sector.
"There was a very strong increase in gross margins which has had a big impact because the newsflow in the sector recently has been all about food deflation," said Dunn.

"They have obviously been negotiating much harder to keep their margins and this would probably be industry-wide. Most people have been expecting margins to decline, but that might not be the case after all," the analyst said.
